summary.summary: This is Cyngor Gwynedd's own 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, still marked 'Subject to Audit', going to the council's Governance and Audit Committee. The balance sheet is solid: long-term borrowing fell from £90.1m to £69.4m over the year, total reserves grew from £592.7m to £644.6m, and the unearmarked General Fund balance nearly doubled from £7.9m to £14.5m after a deliberate top-up. The Capital Financing Requirement rose to £188.5m (from £179.9m) even as external borrowing fell, meaning the council is increasingly relying on internal borrowing rather than new external debt. The narrative notes real budget pressure — a £6.6m in-year overspend concentrated in adult/children's care and waste — but there is no exceptional financial support, capitalisation direction, or section 114-type language anywhere in the document.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd adult services overspent by £6.1m across the three years to 2025-26, committee papers show
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council's adult services department overspent its budget by a total of £6.1 million over the three years to 2025-26, according to a report on the use of data in budget planning put to the Governance and Audit Committee. The figure covers the whole of adult services, not residential care alone.

The report recommends that the lessons learned in adult residential care be applied across all services where spending follows demand. The council's Annual Governance Statement for 2025-26, in which the council speaks about itself, names overspending in both 2024/25 and 2025/26. It gives no amounts for those years.

The statement says setting a balanced budget for 2027/28 will be challenging. It says departmental budgets must be adequate for the level of service required, "to avoid overspending as seen in 2024/25 and 2025/26." It adds that increasing pressures on the budget make it harder for departments to stay within budget. The council also says a situation "can be envisaged" where there are "insufficient funds in the future to address the budget shortfall", and links this to the continuing need to find savings and to rising demand for services. It gives no figure for that shortfall. The statement says the position on day-to-day spending (revenue expenditure) is reported to the Governance and Audit Committee and to the council's Cabinet.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Final report. Use of Data in Budget Planning. Cyngor Gwynedd

news_drafts.headline: North Wales CJC forecasts £39,874 net overspend for 2026/27, with £516,625 on unbudgeted consultants
news_drafts.lead:
The North Wales Corporate Joint Committee (CJC) expects to end 2026/27 with a net overspend of £39,874, according to its July review report before the Governance and Audit Sub-committee on 15 October. The extra cost will be met from reserves, the money the body has set aside, on top of a £624,590 transfer already approved.

The small net figure sits on a larger movement in gross spending. Budgeted expenditure of £1,959,770 is forecast to reach £2,589,644, an overspend of £629,874, or 32%. The main driver is £516,625 on external consultants, against a budget of nothing: £254,400 for programme management, £236,225 for legal work and £26,000 for business advisers. Spending on supplies and services is also forecast to be £435,864 above budget.

Reserves stood at £1,636,007 on 31 March 2026 and are estimated at £971,543 by 31 March 2027. The CJC's statutory finance officer says reserves are expected to be needed for future budgets, as the CJC's resourcing requirements increase and future grants have not been confirmed.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd has £16m of new capital money against £19.76m of requests, and built 118 homes against 247
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council's Cabinet has been told it has about £16m in additional money for capital spending (spending on things that last, such as buildings and flood defences) but requests from education and flood prevention projects come to £19.76m, a gap of £3.76m. The council's Capital Strategy says: "Given that there is currently £16M of additional resource available, it is not possible to fund everything and therefore, there will be a need to prioritise."

The £16m has built up since the council approved its 2024-2034 Asset Plan. It comes from capital grants, receipts, and £3.5m released by de-committing the Health and Care Hub project. The papers do not say which schemes will be funded or dropped.

A separate report to the meeting, the Annual Monitoring Report, covers housing. It records 118 homes completed in the Gwynedd Planning Authority area in 2025/26. That is 129 fewer than the annual average requirement of 247 (52.2% below) and 107 fewer than the forecast trajectory of 225. Since the local plan was adopted in 2017, 2,805 homes have been completed against a trajectory of 3,712, which is 24.4% below.

findings.headline: Renewal and other funds financing rises by £13.329m, including a £12.400m adjustment to the contribution from the Council Tax Premium Fund towards Housing Strategy schemes.
findings.detail: The paper records the largest single adjustment in the revision as the contribution from the Council Tax Premium Fund to the Housing Strategy schemes. Renewal and other funds total £30.770m across the three years.
findings.matters: Reliance on reserves and earmarked funds for capital schemes reduces the cushion available for other pressures, a point finance directors weigh when assessing reserve levels.
findings.figures: Renewal and other funds increase £13.329m; Council Tax Premium Fund adjustment £12.400m; total renewal and other funds £30.770m over three years
findings.quote: Adjustment to the contribution from the Council Tax

findings.headline: Other borrowing rises by £846,000 to fund the renewal of vehicles and equipment.
findings.detail: The only change to borrowing in the revision is £846,000 of additional other borrowing, used for vehicle and equipment renewals in the Highways, Engineering and Consultancy and Environment departments. Supported borrowing is unchanged.
findings.matters: Borrowing for vehicle renewal rather than cash-funded replacement adds to the debt and financing costs that other councils with fleet programmes also carry.
findings.figures: Other borrowing increase £846k (2026/27 and 2028/29 combined over the 3 years 2026/27 to 2028/29 is £7.715m total in table); supported borrowing £12.189m unchanged
findings.quote: Renewal of Vehicles and Equipment by borrowing

findings.headline: Forecast financing costs for 2026/27 are £9.9m, or 2.7% of the net revenue stream, compared with £8.9m and 2.4% in 2025/26.
findings.detail: Financing costs cover interest payable and minimum revenue provision. The forecast falls back to 2.5% in 2027/28 and 2.4% in 2028/29 in the budget figures.
findings.matters: The share of the revenue budget absorbed by financing costs is a direct measure of the revenue cost of capital borrowing, and it is the figure lenders and auditors look at first.
findings.figures: Financing costs £8.9m (2025/26 actual), £9.9m (2026/27 forecast), £9.9m (2027/28), £9.8m (2028/29); proportion of net revenue stream 2.4%, 2.7%, 2.5%, 2.4%

findings.headline: Debt of £81.0m at 31.08.2026 is recorded within the £200m authorised limit and the £190m operational boundary, with the paper stating the council has complied.
findings.detail: The prudential indicators show debt including PFI and leases at £81.0m, with borrowing of £73.9m and PFI and leases of £7.1m. The paper states that debt is below the capital financing requirement and that the council expects to continue to comply.
findings.matters: Headroom between debt and the authorised limit shows how much further borrowing the council could take on, which lenders and finance directors use to judge borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: Debt at 31.08.2026 £81.0m (borrowing £73.9m, PFI and leases £7.1m); authorised limit £200m; operational boundary £190m; CFR forecast 31.3.2027 £192.9m
findings.quote: The Council has complied and expects to continue to comply with this

findings.headline: Welsh Government has withdrawn from the Plas Ogwen scheme, reducing the Welsh Energy Grant by £1.328m.
findings.detail: The paper records a withdrawal of Welsh Government funding from the Plas Ogwen scheme. The adjustment is shown as a reduction of £1,328k in grants and contributions for the Housing and Property Department.
findings.matters: A grant withdrawn mid-scheme leaves the council to fund the gap, and the same risk applies to other councils running energy-efficiency schemes on Welsh Government grant.
findings.quote: Welsh Government has withdrawn from the scheme at Plas Ogwen
